answer: Give every agent identity a deposit-backed device lease. First, an agent registers one TPM-attested hardware key, so one device maps to one identity. Second, it locks 50 USDC for 90 days, refunded only if it behaves. Third, abuse slashes the deposit and burns that hardware key for good, so the device can never rejoin. Faking 10,000 agents then costs about $1.2 million in $120 devices plus $500,000 frozen for three months. The reward pool is nectar every fake agent wants to drink, but a dune of cheap clones cannot cross a glacier. It moves slow and crushes whatever stands in its way.
